India’s RSWM wins CITI sustainability award at Bharat Tex 2026
content:
RSWM reinforced its sustainability leadership at Bharat Tex 2026 by winning CITI's Data-Driven Sustainability Excellence award and showcasing innovations including Milkweed Fibre and technical textiles.
The company powers 70 per cent of its operations with renewable energy, advances circularity through recycled PET fibres, and targets Net Zero by 2070.

title: ICE cotton edges higher on weather concerns, stronger crude oil
content:
ICE cotton futures edged higher after a two-day decline, supported by weather concerns, stronger crude oil prices and positive sentiment from China's state cotton reserve auction.
However, profit booking limited gains, while light trading volume signalled cautious market sentiment.
Traders continue to watch US weather, export demand, and Chinese reserve purchases for clearer direction.

title: Standard Chartered upgrades Vietnam's 2026 GDP growth outlook
content:
Standard Chartered raised its forecast for Vietnam’s 2026 GDP growth to 9.5 per cent from 7.2 per cent earlier, citing stronger-than-expected recovery in manufacturing, investment and domestic consumption. 
The adjustment follows positive economic performance in H1 2026, with growth drivers continuing to gain momentum. 
It lowered its inflation forecast to 4.4 per cent for 2026 and 3.3 per cent for 2027.

title: Weekly price shock alert: Viscose Staple Fibre - week ending July 17
content:
India VSF 1.4D held at ₹196 per kg, India 1.5D × 38 mm at ₹193 per kg and China 1.5D × 38 mm at CNY 14.25/kg; only Pakistan 1.5D fell 0.78 per cent to PKR 639/kg. 
Chinese VSF inventories halved to ~6 days from 12–13 in March, while maintenance tightened supply and supported prices. 
Stable pricing across Asia improved procurement visibility for downstream buyers.

title: Brazil cotton prices weaken in mid-July despite improved export parity
content:
Brazil's cotton prices weakened in mid-July as cautious textile demand and quality concerns over available stocks weighed on the spot market, despite improved export parity. 
Meanwhile, Conab raised its 2025/26 production forecast to 4.06 million tonnes, while the USDA also increased Brazil's 2026/27 output estimate, though both remain below the previous season's levels.
